text: EVO-X2, EVO-X3 and EVO-X1 Pro use soldered memory and cannot be RAM-upgraded.

EVO-X3 (128GB, EUR 3,499.99 on the EU store) uses the same Ryzen AI Max+ 395 as the EVO-X2 and adds OCuLink and a larger triple-fan chassis. The EU EVO-X2 listing extracted was the 64GB model at EUR 1,999.99, so the two prices are for different memory sizes.
EVO-X2 draws 8-14W idle and 147-160W under 70B Q6_K inference, with 41-43 dBA at the test position.
Dense 70B on EVO-X2 runs at single-digit tokens/s (3.7-3.8 at Q6_K); 30B-class MoE Q4 reaches about 86 t/s peak on Vulkan under Linux.
EU store: 2-year warranty, 7-day return, 15% restocking fee on non-defective returns, customer pays return shipping; shorter than the EU 14-day withdrawal right and needs legal check.
EU orders ship primarily from Bremen, Germany; Shenzhen is a fallback and may incur customs duties.

EVO-X2 128GB/2TB retail prices in Austria (EUR 3,999 incl. 19% VAT) and Estonia (EUR 4,450.20 incl. 24% VAT) differ by country, VAT rate and merchant from the official EU 64GB list of EUR 1,999.99, so they cannot be compared directly; no official EU 128GB price was extracted.
Among GMKtec lines seen, only NucBox K11/K8 Plus/M-series appear to take SO-DIMM DDR5; Intel K13/K17/T2 and AMD EVO lines are soldered.
MS-S1 MAX has an internal 320W PSU, 6-heatpipe dual-fan cooling, 2x 10GbE and a PCIe 4.0 x16 slot that runs at x4.
ServeTheHome measured the MS-S1 MAX at about 10 W idle in Windows, 5-6 W without a desktop, and a peak of about 200-220 W in synthetic testing.

Reported speeds for 128GB LPDDR5X-8000 (256 GB/s) systems mix Minisforum and Framework tests and runtimes: 70B dense Q4 about 5 tok/s, 30-35B mixture-of-experts 43-66 tok/s, 120B-class mixture-of-experts roughly 19-31 tok/s. Framework results are not Minisforum measurements.

Minisforum EU list price for MS-S1 MAX 128GB is EUR 3,999.00 against EUR 4,999.00 regular, well above the USD figures from launch-era coverage; memory price inflation is a likely cause but unverified.
Affiliate program pays 2% via AWIN, with a 7 or 30 day cookie (page conflicts).
Standard warranty is 24 months; the 36-month promotion ended 2026-07-31.
Two MS-S1 MAX units clustered run a 235B Q4 model at 10.87 tok/s; the interconnect is not specified in the material read.

For 20+ concurrent CLI agent sessions, CPU cores and RAM matter more than GPU; AI X1 Pro (12C, SO-DIMM up to 96-128GB) is a cheaper agent node than a Strix Halo box, but no concurrency benchmark was found.
Strix Halo (Max+ 395) is 256-bit LPDDR5X-8000, 256 GB/s theoretical; measured real-world about 212-215 GB/s.
DGX Spark (GB10) has 128GB and 273 GB/s, ships DGX OS (Linux).
DGX Spark measured on llama.cpp: gpt-oss-120b MXFP4 tg ~60 t/s, pp ~1956 t/s; Spark is much faster than Strix Halo at prompt processing, comparable token generation at short context.
Strix Halo guidance: about 70 t/s on a 30B-A3B MoE and about 5 t/s on 70B dense. The occasional-70B need is slow on every 256-273 GB/s box.
Apple Mac Studio M5 Max 460/614 GB/s (max 128GB); M5 Ultra 1.2 TB/s (96GB base, 512GB max); Mac mini M5 Pro 307 GB/s max 64GB; M6 153-170 GB/s max 32GB.
Apple NL prices: Mac Studio M5 Max EUR 3,029 (32c GPU/36GB) and 3,689 (40c); M5 Ultra EUR 6,649 and 8,079; Mac mini EUR 1,069 (M6) and 2,019 (M5 Pro), +1,100 for 64GB.
Apple raised Mac mini prices by 300-350 EUR versus the M4 generation.
Framework Desktop 128GB: USD 1,999 to 2,459 on 13 Jan 2026; NL DIY now EUR 3,889 and out of stock.
Corsair AI Workstation 300 128GB: USD 1,999.99 at launch to 2,699.99 from, 3,399.99 max.
DGX Spark rose USD 3,999 to 4,699 in Feb 2026; OEM GB10 boxes USD 5,400-8,200 in Sept 2026 with stock-outs; one EU report EUR 3,680 ex VAT for GX10 1TB.

US list prices of 128GB-class machines rose in 2026: Framework Desktop USD 1,999 to 2,459 (+23%), Corsair AI Workstation 300 USD 1,999.99 to 2,699.99 (+35%), DGX Spark USD 3,999 to 4,699 (+17.5%). These are matched-product US list prices; no cause is established here.
TrendForce expects 4Q26 conventional DRAM +10-15% QoQ and NAND +15-20% QoQ, supply tight into 2027.
DDR5-6400 128GB kit went from USD 329 low to USD 3,399 (18 Aug 2026).
RTX 5090 EU street above EUR 5,000, 32GB; RTX PRO 6000 96GB EUR 15,490 lowest; R9700 32GB EUR 1,545.
Medusa Halo (Ryzen AI Max 500) RUMOR: LPDDR6, 256-bit about 460 GB/s, Zen 6/RDNA 5, 2027-2028; AMD has not confirmed.

Strix Halo software: Vulkan via llama.cpp/LM Studio recommended on Windows and Linux; ROCm immature; Linux needs kernel 6.15+. A Windows 96GB VGM cap on 128GB machines and Linux GTT tuning appeared only in search snippets and are unverified.
Framework 192GB (Max+ PRO 495, 273 GB/s) allows up to 160GB to iGPU; ships Fedora, Windows 11 supported; ships Nov 2026.
Apple GPU wired memory limit can be raised via sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb.
Dense 405B on M5 Ultra gets about 2.9 t/s; bandwidth decides speed, capacity decides what loads.
HP Z2 Mini G1a 128GB/1TB EUR 3,215 ex VAT / 3,890.15 incl VAT at a Dutch reseller (ships when available).

A community wiki (no counting method stated) estimates about 90% of Chinese Strix Halo PCs, including GMKtec, Bosgame, FEVM, Corsair and NIMO, use the Sixunited platform. Its hardware page lists the GMKtec EVO-X2 with the Sixunited AXB35-02 board.
Framework NL mainboard prices incl. VAT: 385/32GB EUR 1,079; 395/64GB EUR 1,859; 395/128GB EUR 3,539.
Framework 128GB desktop rose from USD 1,999 launch to USD 2,459 on 12 Jan 2026 due to the RAM crisis; Framework said it would cut prices when the market calms.
Bosgame EU listed M5 395 128GB/2TB at EUR 2,439.95 on 24 Jun 2026 (was 2,875.95).
Framework Desktop uses a semi-custom FSP 400W Flex ATX PSU and a Cooler Master and Noctua thermal system.
EU EUR 3 duty per item category applies on parcels up to EUR 150 from 1 July 2026 until 1 July 2028; it does not cover a 128GB mini PC priced in the thousands.
EU consumers have a 2-year minimum legal guarantee from the seller; a shorter brand warranty (for example 12 months) does not replace it for consumer sales.
A single-unit Alibaba price for a Strix Halo 128GB machine (snippet USD 3,027-3,107) is not below EU retail, so direct sourcing gives no price edge for one unit.
Minisforum MS-S1 Max uses an internal Lite-On 320W PSU and soldered 128GB LPDDR5X; review sample shipped with a 2TB Kingston QLC SSD.
Lemonade runs on Windows 11, Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian, Arch, macOS and Docker, with Vulkan, ROCm and NPU (flm, ryzenai-llm) backends, gfx1151 listed, and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
FastFlowLM supports XDNA2 NPUs on Windows and Linux with an OpenAI-compatible server and free commercial use of its kernels.
On Strix Halo Linux, Vulkan was faster than HIP/ROCm on llama-bench (May 2025), while HIP+WMMA+FlashAttention reached 60.29 t/s on a 30B MoE (July 2025). Backend choice is model-dependent.

Linux can address about 124GB of 128GB as GPU memory via amdgpu.gttsize and ttm.pages_limit; Windows is reported capped at 96GB via Variable Graphics Memory. The Windows figure comes from a secondary blog and an unopened AMD search snippet.

Windows 11 restarts after updates outside active hours (default 8-17); Microsoft says the 'no auto-restart with logged on users' policy does not work as described and many restart policies are legacy for Windows 11. Agent sessions need a supervisor that survives reboots.
WSL2 defaults to 50% of host RAM, NAT networking and a 60s VM idle timeout.
Tailscale Personal is free for up to 6 users with unlimited devices; paid tiers are USD 8 and 18 per user per month.

Netherlands new-card prices around 2026-10-03: RTX 5090 from EUR 5,499; RTX 5080 from 1,649; RTX 5070 Ti from 1,181; RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 19,999; Radeon AI PRO R9700 1,876; Arc Pro B60 799. RTX 4090 new listings 3,790-3,990 (2026-09-28).

Cloud GPU hourly (USD): RunPod 5090 0.69-0.99, 4090 0.34-0.74, RTX PRO 6000 1.69-2.09, A100 80GB 1.19-1.59, H100 PCIe 1.99-2.89; Lambda H100 PCIe 3.29; Modal H100 about 3.95; Vast 5090 from about 0.47.

Break-even arithmetic (mine, USD/EUR parity ignored): a EUR 5,499 RTX 5090 equals about 5,555 secure-cloud hours at 0.99 or about 7,970 community hours at 0.69; at 8 h/day that is roughly 1.9 to 2.7 years of daily use before power and host costs. Buying wins only if the GPU runs most days for 2+ years or privacy/latency matters; otherwise rent.
Strix Halo 128GB reportedly gives 8-12 t/s on 70B dense Q4 and 60-86 t/s on a 30B MoE (secondary sources, 2025-2026).
APC Back-UPS BX1600MI (1600VA/900W) costs EUR 220 incl VAT at dectdirect.nl.
Minisforum pays 2% commission with a 30-day cookie, on Awin, Impact and Webgains; DE programme excludes VAT and postage and closes PPC.
Apple's current affiliate programme (Performance Partners via Partnerize) covers digital content and subscriptions only, with 30-day cookie and 60-90 day payment.
Minisforum accepts B2B wholesale applications from 10 units with 3-year extended warranty; Beelink offers ODM/OEM and positions as system integrator.
Amazon fee schedule reads for amazon.nl and amazon.de disagree on electronics (6% vs 5%); verify inside an approved account.
Awin does not accept #affiliate or #partner as disclosure; #Ad is required.
Awin (34.8%) is the leading affiliate network in the Netherlands, ahead of Impact (13.2%).
Framework says the Desktop runs 300B-class models at 4-bit quantisation.
Tailscale Personal plan is free with up to 6 users and unlimited user devices; Standard is $8 and Premium $18 per user per month.
cloudflared on Windows does not auto-update; exe and MSI are provided.
Windows 11 Home cannot host incoming Remote Desktop; Pro, Enterprise, Education can.
Hyper-V on Windows 11 is included in Pro, Enterprise and Education.
Docker Desktop is free for businesses with fewer than 250 employees and less than $10M annual revenue.
Backblaze B2 is $6.95/TB/month with free egress up to 3x stored data, then $0.01/GB.
Infisical free tier is 5 identities and 3 environments; Pro is $20 per identity per month billed yearly.
Proxmox VE is AGPL; Community subscription is EUR120 per CPU socket per year.
Wan2.2 TI2V-5B needs at least 24GB VRAM and A14B at least 80GB on a single GPU.
HunyuanVideo needs 60GB (720p, 129 frames) or 45GB (540p) minimum, 80GB recommended, on Linux with NVIDIA CUDA.
GMKtec lists OCuLink PCIe Gen4 x4 on K8 Plus, K11, K12, M7 Ultra and USB4 at 40 Gbps.
On Linux the default GTT limit is about 50% of RAM and can be raised via TTM pages_limit.
The Windows 96GB GPU memory cap versus Linux ~124GB is not confirmed by a primary page.
Universal Control supports one Mac plus up to two other Mac or iPad devices on the same Apple Account.
A search digest of Notebookcheck's MS-S1 Max reviews reports 9-12 W idle, about 120 W under AI inference and 43 dBA under load (page not opened).

The 2026 Combined Nomenclature (Implementing Regulation 2025/1926) shows 'Free' in the conventional duty column for CN 8471 30 00, 41 00, 49 00 and 50 00. Live TARIC measures for Chinese origin were not retrievable.
Douane says Dutch import VAT is usually 21%; the Belastingdienst article 23 permit lets an entrepreneur defer import VAT to the next VAT return.
Council Regulation 2026/382 Article 2 sets a EUR 3 duty per item for consignments with an intrinsic value up to EUR 150, from 1 July 2026 to 1 July 2028.

Directive 2011/83/EU gives a consumer 14 days to withdraw from a distance contract, defines a consumer as acting outside trade or business, and bars waiver; Your Europe says the rules do not apply when selling to other businesses.

GMKtec's German shipping policy says: 'Um die Zollkosten zu reduzieren, deklarieren wir in der Regel einen niedrigeren Warenwert' (to reduce customs costs we generally declare a lower goods value), for shipments from China; it describes shipping from the German warehouse as avoiding extra EU taxes.

GMKtec's FAQ states a 60-calendar-day return window from shipment and a 15% restocking fee on non-fault returns; the warranty is stated as two years (German page). Other GMKtec pages in the research stated 7 days and 1 year, so its own terms conflict.

AMD states Variable Graphics Memory allows up to 96 GB of GPU memory on a 128GB Ryzen AI Max+ 395 under Windows (Adrenalin 25.8.1+); seen as a search excerpt and a secondary article. Open LM Studio and llama.cpp issues report Vulkan loads failing or stalling near 64 GB with 96 GB set.
Microsoft Learn: Windows 11 Home cannot install the Hyper-V role and cannot host incoming Remote Desktop connections; BitLocker enablement is listed for Pro, Enterprise and Education.
Microsoft Store NL lists Windows 11 Home at EUR 145.00 and Pro at EUR 259.00 (USB, Dutch); the pages do not state VAT.
Minisforum's product page lists two USB4 v2 ports at 80 Gbps (rear) and two USB4 ports at 40 Gbps (front), two 10GbE ports, a PCIe x16 slot running at PCIe 4.0 x4 and a built-in 320 W PSU.

Notebookcheck's review of the 64GB EVO-X2 says its iGPU can take up to 48 GB and leave 16 GB for the system. ServeTheHome's 70B Q6_K test needed over 50 GB of GPU memory on the 128GB unit. No independent LLM speed test of the 64GB EVO-X2 was found.
Reported EVO-X2 noise under load ranges from 41-43 dBA (ServeTheHome, 128GB) to about 50 dBA (a snippet of a 3DTested review) and 'annoying' at high TDP (Wccftech); the conflict is unresolved.

OCuLink is PCIe 4.0 x4 (about 8 GB/s theoretical). A gaming-test comparison (Guru3D citing Try Some Tech) measured about 6.7 GB/s over OCuLink and about 5.8 GB/s over Thunderbolt 5; this is gaming data, not AI inference.

One reported setup (MindStudio blog, secondary): an RTX 5080 16GB over OCuLink on a Strix Halo mini PC, Vulkan in LM Studio, ran about 3 times the iGPU on models that fit in 16GB and 1.6 tok/s when the model exceeded VRAM. The post states no model names or test conditions beyond that.

The same blog reports an RTX Pro 6000 96GB over OCuLink at 69 tok/s on a 32B dense model and 121 tok/s on a 122B mixture-of-experts model, and 37-38 tok/s when the 122B model was split across the GPU and the iGPU, which it attributes to the OCuLink link.

Level1Techs forum reports on Windows 11 Pro with a Strix Halo iGPU plus a dGPU describe instability and 35-40% slowdowns, LM Studio 0.3.16 missing the iGPU when a dGPU was present, and an improvement after capping iGPU VRAM at 512MB in the BIOS. These are forum reports.

In the reported runs, two-node llama.cpp RPC over direct USB4 (about 9.4 Gbps, Linux) gave 15.35 tok/s on MiniMax-M2.5-REAP-139B and 12.6 tok/s on Qwen3.5-397B (owner benchmarks), against single-node results of 42.7 tok/s on an 80B-A3B and 86.1 tok/s on a 30B-A3B model. A four-node Framework test over 5GbE by Jeff Geerling reached about 8.25 tok/s on DeepSeek R1 Q2_K_M, the same as one node, and its author recommends scaling vertically; the method is described as experimental, with segfaults on some quants. These runs differ in model, quantisation and setup, so they do not establish a general rule.
